subject: START statement
notes:
kb/Work PB354. RULE (--check 14.9.41.3 4): 'Data-name-1 or record-key-name-1 shall not be subject to any OCCURS clauses.' The rule has two operand legs (indexed and relative) and they behave differently.
INDEXED LEG -- ENFORCED, but only as a SIDE EFFECT and reported under the WRONG RULE. RecordLayout.OffsetOf bails to null when the item or any ancestor carries OCCURS ('if (p.Occurs is not null) return null;   // subject to OCCURS => no single fixed position'), so KeyIndexByPosition returns null and BindStart emits COBOL0862 '<name> neither names a record key nor begins at the leftmost character position of one with a length not greater than that key (ISO 14.9.41 SR6)'. PROBED (out-b1/probe/sr4-occ) with '05 IX-KEY. 10 IX-ELEM PIC X(3) OCCURS 2 TIMES.' and 'START IXF KEY IS = IX-ELEM (1)': rejected with exactly that message. The source IS refused, so no illegal program compiles -- but the message asserts something FALSE about this operand: IX-ELEM(1) DOES begin at IX-KEY's leftmost character position and IS shorter than it. The rule actually violated is SR4; OffsetOf's null collapses two distinct rejection reasons into one sentence, and a user reading it would look for the wrong problem.
RELATIVE LEG -- NO CHECK AT ALL. BindStart's relative arm tests only ReferenceEquals(operand.Item, file.RelativeKeyItem) (that is SR5), which is TRUE for a SUBSCRIPTED reference to the same DataItem. PROBED (same file): with '01 WS-RKT. 05 WS-RK PIC 9(4) OCCURS 3 TIMES.' and 'RELATIVE KEY IS WS-RK', the statement 'START RLF KEY IS = WS-RK (2)' compiles with NO diagnostic. That shape is reachable only through a file control entry that already violates 12.4.5.13.3 SR1 (--check: 'Data-name-1 shall not be subject to any OCCURS clauses') -- and the keyed binder's file screen of that day implemented 12.4.5.13's SR2 (unsigned integer, no P) and SR3 (not within a record of the file) but NOT its SR1, so nothing anywhere in the chain diagnoses it. The two missing checks cover for each other.
UNDER-REJECTS. TEST: none.

LANDED 2026-09-05 (kb/Work PB354). SR4 has its own named check, on BOTH arms, ahead of the position walk: RecordLayout.IsSubjectToOccurs is the one predicate for the phrase "subject to an OCCURS clause" and BindStart calls it before either organization arm. The indexed leg no longer reports an OCCURS violation under SR6's message (a sentence that was FALSE of an operand which does begin at the key's leftmost position), and the relative leg - which never called OffsetOf and therefore had no check at all - now reports it too. Both legs are pinned by their own negative fixture. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/KeyedIoBinder.cs#KeyedValidateFile (KeyedValidateFile was removed when the file-control KEY rules became one table, FileControlKeyRules (kb/Work PB699, 3c5b4cd4d))
